QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_5

question.text: Which SEBI-defined open-ended debt mutual fund category is mandated to invest in overnight securities having a maturity of ONE BUSINESS DAY, making it the category with the lowest interest-rate and credit risk among debt mutual fund categories?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the SEBI debt fund categorisation referenced in the workbook (pp. 38 and 50), the OVERNIGHT FUND category is specifically defined as one that invests in overnight securities with maturity of ONE business day. Because the underlying instruments mature daily, the category carries the lowest interest-rate and credit risk among debt fund categories. The stem now precisely targets this SEBI definition, so option A is uniquely correct. The Trap: Liquid Funds (option B) invest in securities up to 91 days - low risk but not one-business-day. Ultra Short Duration (option C) has Macaulay duration 3-6 months. Money Market Funds (option D) invest in money-market instruments up to 1 year. None match the one-business-day SEBI definition. Note: The original stem asked for the "highest combination of safety and liquidity with minimal return", which the workbook (p. 290) directly assigns to Liquid Funds for lowest-risk suitability, making both Overnight and Liquid defensible. The stem has been re-anchored to the SEBI category DEFINITION (one-business-day maturity) so the keyed answer is uniquely Overnight Fund. Source: NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook, pp. 38, 50.
